newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan may state its forex stance at G7 meeting - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan may state its forex stance at G7 meeting - MOF.

text.p: Japan will clearly state its stance on foreign exchange rates at a meeting of the Group of Seven (G7) industrial nations this weekend if necessary, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Wednesday.
He said Japan will call for stability in exchange rates.
"Currency stability is extremely important for the world and Japanese economies. An excessively weak or strong yen is not favourable," he said.
"The six other G7 members will make their own judgment on foreign exchange rates and Japan will make clear its stance if necessary," Mitsuzuka said.
Asked about Wednesday's market rumours in Tokyo about the financial health of Nippon Credit Bank, he said the ministry's full support for the bank remained unchanged.
"The ministry has had no worries about the bank. It (the bank) is doing its utmost to improve its management. We don't believe that the bank will collapse as said in some media reports."
He added the ministry was exchanging information with the bank daily.
"The data (of the bank) is different now from what it was a month or two ago," he said.
